dimensions.detail: The artifacts consistently describe a local-first research vault that stores project state in SQLite, ingests user-selected web content, supports search-backed verification, and offers optional portal, watchdog, and MCP services.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Most side effects are user-invoked or visibly exposed in the UI/CLI, though some convenience flows can mutate local research state automatically, such as default auto-seeding and discovery auto-planning.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is standard Python editable install; no services start at install time. The portal and optional services require explicit commands.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Network access, API keys, subprocess execution, and local database reads/writes are proportionate to the research-orchestration purpose and are substantially documented, with SSRF blocking enabled by default.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill persists SQLite data, portal state, PID files, and a portal auth token file; this is disclosed and the token file is chmod 600, but users should treat it as a local credential.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The skill documents its environment variables, local database use, shell commands, networking, portal, watchdog, and MCP features; these capabilities fit the stated purpose.
[TP4] expected: The portal, authentication token, CORS settings, scraping, search APIs, exports, and subprocess-backed CLI wrapper are disclosed as manual opt-in components rather than hidden behavior.
[SDI-1] expected: Diagnostics expose local operational metadata to authenticated portal users; useful for troubleshooting, but users should avoid exposing the portal beyond trusted localhost access.
[SDI-2] expected: Developer-mode actions can mutate research state, but they are labeled as advanced/dev actions and require portal authentication.
[SDI-2] expected: The private-network fetch option is a real SSRF-sensitive control, but it is off by default and labeled in the UI/CLI as an SSRF risk.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Opening the discovery view can auto-create verification plans; this is a local state mutation and a usability shortcut, not evidence of malicious behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Authenticated users can trigger URL ingestion and search result caching; this is core research functionality and is mediated by typed backend routes and SSRF checks.
[EA2] expected: Strategy execution requires an explicit execute flag and is limited to verification/synthesis paths; it does not silently run arbitrary recommendations.
[SQP-2] expected: The portal token persists in .portal_auth for reuse and is documented, chmod 600, and only generated during manual portal startup.
[SC4] expected: The flagged dependencies are expected for the portal and networking features; the lockfile resolves Vite and PostCSS to newer versions than the manifest floors, while Python dependencies should still be pinned/audited by users.
[SDI-1] expected: The optional AI summary path is user-invoked with --ai; it may send project context to an OpenClaw agent process, so it is a privacy consideration rather than hidden exfiltration.
llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a local research vault that can fetch user-supplied URLs, use configured search APIs, and run a localhost portal. Keep the portal bound to localhost, protect or delete .portal_auth when needed, leave private-network fetching disabled unless you intentionally need it, and avoid using --ai or search/watchdog features with sensitive research unless you accept those data flows.
llm.summary: This is a disclosed local research tool with optional web fetching and portal features; its main risks are operational configuration choices rather than hidden or malicious behavior.
